text:
People Ops: Thanks for the great turnout at today's all-hands Q&A! Drop any follow-ups about reviews, leveling, promotions, comp, or benefits here and we'll answer in-thread. :sparkles:

Sam K: Quick ops question: when will the official review feedback be visible in Lattice? I saw managers were drafting notes.

People Ops: Managers should submit final feedback by end of day Wednesday. Once submitted, Lattice will unlock view permissions within ~24 hours. If you still can't see it after that, ping us and we'll check permissions.

Evelyn R: Is there guidance for managers on consolidating peer feedback? Some managers are getting a lot of short messages and it's inconsistent.

Dani (People Ops Intern): We put together a short guide this morning: "How to synthesize peer feedback" 12 bullet tips + example excerpts. Link: https://intranet.redwood.example/manager-guides/synthesize-feedback

Hector (Eng): Promotion timing question: if someone hits the bar mid-cycle and their manager requests a promo now, would the comp bump be effective immediately or at next payroll? Need to coordinate with an offer we're making.

Comp Committee Bot: Promo processing: effective date = manager proposed date (must be within the current fiscal quarter). Salary changes processed at next payroll; however retro pay can be issued for prior pay periods when approved. Please include payroll case in request.

Sam K: If a manager wants to nominate someone for an out-of-cycle merit because of market pressure, what benchmarks do they need?

Maya (CTO): For market-based adjustments include 1) comparator role examples (public salary data or benchmark decks), 2) evidence of retention risk, and 3) a short business impact statement. Comp partners will review and advise.

Evelyn R: Requesting more clarity on leveling language. The IC rubric items around "scale" vs "scope" are confusing.

People Ops: Noted. We're updating the rubric to add concrete examples for "scale" (number of users/requests, complexity of systems) and "scope" (cross-team ownership, product outcomes). Draft will be shared by Friday; comments welcome.

Hector (Eng): Appeals  I submitted an appeal last cycle but didn't get status updates. What's the SLA for appeals?

People Ops: Appeals SLA: initial triage within 3 business days, full decision within 10 business days for performance/leveling appeals. Compensation appeals that need committee review may take up to 21 days. We'll follow up on your open case today.

Sam K: PTO/holidays: any change to the summer flex week mentioned in the deck?

People Ops: Summer flex week remains opt-in. Managers approve based on team coverage. Also reminder: carryover cap = 10 days; exceptions require manager sign-off + People Ops approval.

Evelyn R: Do we keep the "promotion readiness" checklist for managers? Where is it?

Dani (People Ops Intern): Yes 12 checklist is live at: https://intranet.redwood.example/promo-readiness-checklist. It includes example artifacts to attach (PRs, design proposals, customer comms).

Maya (CTO): One note on bias mitigation: during calibration we'd like managers to surface concrete success metrics (OKRs, incident reductions, adoption numbers) rather than adjectives. That helps make decisions objective.

Comp Committee Bot: Reminder: use the promo template when submitting: 1) summary, 2) impact examples, 3) proposed band + comp, 4) evidence links. Template: https://intranet.redwood.example/templates/promo-template

People Ops: We'll compile today's thread into a short FAQ and post to the handbook. If you want a private conversation, book People Ops office hours: https://calendar.redwood.example/peopleops-officehours. Closing thread 12 keep the Qs coming and thanks for the constructive feedback! :clap:
